adjudication_records.issue_text: `{{#unless automatic}}` in group_member.hbs is evaluated in the item-view context where `automatic` is undefined, so the remove link renders for automatic group members and the DELETE fails with a 422 can_not_modify_automatic error

findMembers' empty-name branch changed from returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` to a bare `return;`, breaking the thenable contract and causing TypeError for any caller chaining `.then()` on the result
GroupMembersController never sets `members`, so the public `/groups/:name/members` template iterates over nothing and renders an empty table
Public members page has no pagination controls while `groups_controller.rb#members` caps results at 50, silently hiding members past the first 50

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` to always paginate with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50)` and `offset`, and returns only `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)` plus `meta.total`. On the public members page, the route `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets `model` to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, and the template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}` (i.e., the group’s `members` property populated by `findMembers`). However, unlike the admin group template (which adds next/previous controls), no pagination UI or actions are added for the public members template/route to change `offset` and fetch subsequent pages. As a result, only the first 50 members are shown with no controls to access the rest, silently hiding members beyond 50.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `add_members` in admin groups controller silently skips nonexistent usernames and returns success_json, giving admins no feedback for misspelled usernames

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. If a username is misspelled/nonexistent, it is simply ignored (no errors collected). The action then calls `group.save` and renders `success_json` even if zero users were added, giving the caller no indication that some/all usernames were invalid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `totalPages` calculation `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` is wrong when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, producing a phantom empty page
matched_golden_ids: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly flags the same pagination bug: using Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 overcounts when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, creating an extra/empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `findMembers` offset is clamped against stale `user_count` and the server does not clamp offset to total, so removing a member on the last page leaves currentPage beyond totalPages showing e.g. "5/4"
`remove_member` doesn't validate that user_id is a member and returns success_json without verifying the join row was actually deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds, without checking whether the user was actually a member or whether any join row was deleted. However, this behavior is not clearly incorrect: removing a non-member can be intentionally idempotent (and the previous implementation also removed members without validating membership and returned success). The diff does not establish a requirement that it must error when `user_id` is not a member, so calling this a definite bug is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `addMembers` in admin-group.js.es6 never clears the input after a successful add and has no error handling on the returned promise

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action only checks `Em.isEmpty(this.get("usernames"))` and then calls `this.get("model").addMembers(...)` without clearing `usernames` afterward. The code even contains `// TODO: should clear the input`, confirming the behavior. Also, `model.addMembers` returns the `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` promise, but `addMembers` neither returns that promise nor attaches any `.then`/`.catch` handling, so errors/success aren’t handled at this call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No spec coverage for the public `members` endpoint's pagination contract (meta: total/limit/offset), and `params[:limit]` of 0 or negative is passed straight to `.limit(0)`, returning no members with total > 0

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination parameters are taken directly from the request: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then used as `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamping/validation for `limit <= 0`, so a request with `?limit=0` (or negative) will produce `members` as an empty list while `meta.total` is still the real count (`total = group.users.count`), which is an inconsistent/likely unintended result introduced by this change. Also, the diff adds a new response contract (`render json: { members: ..., meta: { total/limit/offset } }`) but the only specs touched are `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`; no spec is added/updated for the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint to verify the `meta` pagination contract.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Controller spec uses xhr :put :remove_member but the route defined is a DELETE route, so the tests will raise an unrecognized-route error and never exercise the action
matched_golden_ids: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue points out the same mismatch: the test sends an XHR PUT request to remove_member while the route is defined to accept DELETE for that action, leading to routing errors and the action not being exercised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Shared form styling block in admin_base.scss includes .badges selector unrelated to the stated intent of group membership handling

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a SCSS rule `.groups, .badges { .form-horizontal { ... } }`, which applies the same form styling to both the groups and badges admin areas. Including `.badges` is not a verifiable defect: it doesn’t break functionality, introduce a correctness/security issue, or contradict any behavior shown in the diff. At most it’s a stylistic/organizational concern about selector scope/intent, which is not a “real problem” per the criteria.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New update action in admin/groups_controller.rb drops support for membership changes via PUT /admin/groups/:id, silently breaking existing API callers with no test asserting the breakage or deprecation

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Admin::GroupsController#update to only update alias_level, visible, and (non-automatic) name. Previously, update_put read params[:group] and applied payload[:usernames] to group.usernames (enabling membership changes via PUT /admin/groups/:id). That logic is removed, and membership mutations are moved to new add_members/remove_member endpoints (PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members). Because #update still returns success_json on save and simply ignores any usernames data, existing callers using PUT /admin/groups/:id with usernames would no longer modify membership and would not get an error (silent behavior). The updated specs also drop the old “update group members” test and instead test add_members, so there’s no test asserting backward compatibility or deprecation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers in group.js no longer returns a promise for nameless/new groups (returns undefined instead of Ember.RSVP.resolve([])), breaking the promise-returning invariant
matched_golden_ids: Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to a code path in the function that does not explicitly return a value, resulting in `undefined` being returned. The candidate adds that this breaks the expected promise-returning behavior (should return `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`), which is a direct consequence of the missing return noted in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unversioned breaking API change: groups members endpoint response shape changed from bare array to object with members/meta envelope, breaking existing consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which produces a bare JSON array) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e. an object envelope with `members` and `meta`. This is a verifiable response-shape change for the same endpoint (`/groups/:group_id/members(.json)`), and although the Ember client in this diff is updated to consume `result.members`/`result.meta`, any other existing consumers expecting the prior bare array will break. No versioning/backward-compat handling is shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route removed: GET /admin/groups/:group_id/users deleted with no replacement or deprecation, causing 404s for existing clients

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the member route `get "users"` under `admin/groups` in `config/routes.rb`, but the finding’s claim that it was removed “with no replacement or deprecation” and will “cause 404s for existing clients” is not directly verifiable from the diff. The change introduces new endpoints for membership management (`PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members`) and group member listing is now served via `GET /groups/:group_id/members.json` (non-admin). The diff also updates the admin UI/model code away from the old mechanism, and there’s no evidence in the diff of remaining callers to `/admin/groups/:group_id/users`. Thus the “causing 404s for existing clients” part is speculative/out-of-scope for a strict diff-based defect claim.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PATCH-based incremental membership API (update_patch handling changes add/delete) deleted with no replacement, so memberships can no longer be modified via PUT /admin/groups/:id

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-based `update_patch` incremental membership handling and also removes membership updates from `PUT /admin/groups/:id` (no more `group.usernames` in `update`). However, membership modification is explicitly replaced by new endpoints and routes: `PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` -> `add_members` and `DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members` -> `remove_member`, and the JS model/controller is updated to call these (`addMembers`, `removeMember`). Therefore the statement "deleted with no replacement" is not verifiable from the diff; only the narrower claim that membership can’t be modified via `PUT /admin/groups/:id` is true but appears intentional and replaced elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops unknown usernames and reports success even when zero members were added, with input not cleared so failure is invisible; the spec covering silent failure was deleted rather than replaced with error reporting

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are processed via `usernames.split(",").each` and only added when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; unknown usernames are simply skipped with no error or warning. The action then calls `group.save` and returns `success_json` on success, which will still be true even if zero users were added (e.g., all usernames unknown), so the request reports success despite doing nothing. On the client side, `addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6` contains `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not clear `this.get("usernames")`, making the no-op effectively invisible. Additionally, the prior specs that explicitly asserted “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” were removed with the old PATCH-based incremental update tests, and no new spec replaces this behavior with error reporting for unknown usernames.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty, breaking callers that chain .then()

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` was changed from `return Ember.RSVP.resolve([]);` when `name` is empty to `return ;`, which returns `undefined`. This is a real behavioral regression: the method no longer consistently returns a promise-like value, so any caller that does `group.findMembers().then(...)` (as the removed `afterModel` hooks previously did) would now throw when `name` is blank. Even though the updated callers in this diff no longer chain `.then`, the method’s contract is still broken for empty-name cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination off-by-one: totalPages and currentPage calculations are wrong when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, showing an extra empty page
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same edge case: when total user_count is an exact multiple of the page limit, the pagination logic allows navigating to an offset equal to the total, resulting in an extra/empty last page (confusing UX). The candidate frames it as totalPages/currentPage miscalculation, but the underlying issue (empty page at the end) matches the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: After deleting the last member of the last page, findMembers clamps offset using stale pre-deletion user_count, resulting in an empty page

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Discourse.Group#findMembers`, the request offset is clamped using the *current* `user_count` before the AJAX call: `offset = Math.min(this.get("user_count"), Math.max(this.get("offset"), 0));`. When `removeMember` succeeds it calls `self.findMembers()` without first adjusting `offset` or `user_count`. If you delete the last member on the last page (e.g., `user_count` was 51, `limit` 50, `offset` 50), the pre-request clamp still sends `offset=50`. The server will then return `meta.total=50` and `members=[]` (since offset equals total), leaving the UI on an empty page. The code does not correct `offset` after receiving the new total either; it just sets `offset` to `result.meta.offset`, which remains 50.

adjudication_records.issue_text: params[:limit] is uncapped client input on a public route, allowing expensive full-list materialization queries (no MAX_LIMIT clamp)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and then uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit)`. There is no MAX_LIMIT clamp or other upper bound, and this is a non-admin/public controller (guarded only by `ensure_can_see!`). A client can request an arbitrarily large `limit`, causing the server to fetch and serialize a very large member list, which is an expensive query/response and a plausible DoS vector. The prior code implicitly constrained this in some cases (automatic groups) with a default 200; the new code still lacks any cap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query: User.find_by_username called in a loop for each username in add_members

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and inside the loop executes `User.find_by_username(username)`. That results in one DB query per username provided (plus later `group.save`), which is a classic N+1/per-item query pattern and is directly verifiable from the diff. It could be optimized by fetching all users in a single query (e.g., `User.where(username: list)` or `where(username_lower: ...)`) before adding them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member relies on group.users.delete(user_id) plus group.save side effects; save returns true regardless of whether the delete matched, so no real invariant is checked

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which immediately removes the association row in the database) and then calls `group.save`. That `save` does not “confirm” that a membership was actually removed; it will typically return `true` because the group record itself wasn’t changed and remains valid. However, this doesn’t introduce a clear correctness/security bug: removing a non-member is commonly treated as an idempotent success, and if the underlying `delete` failed at the DB level it would raise rather than return false and be caught by `group.save`. So the finding is more of a redundancy/misleading-check nit than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: update action accepts params[:name] without stripping whitespace, diverging from the create path's validation for the same column

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#create the group name is normalized with `(params[:name] || '').strip`, but in Admin::GroupsController#update it assigns `group.name = params[:name] if params[:name] && !group.automatic` with no `.strip`. This creates an inconsistency where updating a group can persist leading/trailing whitespace in `name` even though creation prevents it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: asJSON() no longer includes usernames and server update/create no longer read params[:group][:usernames], silently dropping membership changes from API consumers and making one-step group creation with members impossible

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes support for sending usernames as part of group create/update. On the client side, `Discourse.Group#asJSON` no longer includes `usernames`, and the controller no longer calls `saveWithUsernames/createWithUsernames` (it now calls `save/create`). On the server side, `Admin::GroupsController#create` now reads `params[:name]`/`params[:visible]` (not `params[:group][:usernames]`), and `update` no longer applies any `usernames` parameter at all. Membership changes are only possible via the new `add_members`/`remove_member` endpoints, so any existing callers still sending `group[usernames]` will have that input ignored (i.e., membership changes are dropped) and one-step create-with-members is no longer possible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page defaults to limit=50 with no pagination controls, so groups with more than 50 members silently show only the first 50 to regular users

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes member retrieval to always apply pagination: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = ...limit(limit).offset(offset)`, returning only that slice plus `meta`. On the public members route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`), it now calls `model.findMembers()` which requests `/groups/:name/members.json` with the model’s `limit` (default `50`) and `offset` (default `0`). The public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` was updated to iterate `{{#each m in members}}`, but no pagination UI/controls were added there in this diff (pagination controls were only added to the admin group template). Therefore, for regular users, groups with >50 members will display only the first 50 with no obvious way to page through the rest, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group_member.hbs references 'automatic' which is undefined on the User item context, so the remove link always renders even for automatic groups
removeMember has no error handler, so when the server rejects removal from an automatic group with 422 can_not_modify_automatic, the member stays listed with no feedback
alias_level and visible are applied unconditionally to automatic groups in the new update controller, loosening the automatic-group non-modifiable protection invariant while name is still guarded

adjudication.rationale: In the previous implementation, `update_put(group)` set `group.alias_level` and `group.visible` before checking `group.automatic`, and only guarded renaming/membership changes for automatic groups. The new `update` method preserves that same behavior: it always applies `alias_level` and `visible`, and only guards `name` when `group.automatic`. Therefore the diff does not newly “loosen” automatic-group immutability for `alias_level`/`visible`; that was already allowed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unvalidated limit/offset on public members endpoint (groups_controller.rb:22-24): no upper bound or sign check allows limit=100000000 causing server to serialize entire membership of any visible group in one response

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` and then directly applies them in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound and no validation for negative values. This allows a client to request an extremely large `limit` (or even a negative limit like `-1`, which in PostgreSQL effectively removes the limit) and potentially force serialization of the entire member list in one response, creating a clear DoS/data-exposure risk for groups the requester is allowed to see.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Negative limit value passed straight into AR's limit() with undefined behavior

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is used directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit)`. If a client supplies `limit=-10`, `to_i` yields `-10` and that negative value is passed straight into ActiveRecord's `limit()`, with no validation/clamping in the diff. This is a concrete, verifiable path from untrusted input to `limit()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.users.count plus the query run twice amplifies the cost of the over-fetch

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the code does execute two separate DB queries: `total = group.users.count` (COUNT(*)) and then a paginated SELECT for `members`. This is standard pagination behavior to return both the current page and the total size, and it does not “over-fetch” rows (COUNT doesn’t load the user records). While it may add some overhead, it’s not a clear defect/bug introduced by the diff—just an expected tradeoff for providing `meta.total`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: usernames.split(",") on a possibly-array param causes a 500 error path

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members the code does `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` then `usernames.split(",")`. That would indeed raise if `usernames` were an Array, but nothing in the diff shows the parameter being sent as an array. The JS side (`addMembers`) passes `data: { usernames: usernames }` where `usernames` is the value bound to `{{user-selector usernames=usernames}}`, and the prior implementation explicitly built a comma-separated string (via `.join(',')`), strongly indicating this field is intended to be a string. The new spec for add_members also passes a comma-joined string. So the finding relies on an unproven assumption about input shape rather than a verifiable defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:~92 uses xhr :put, :remove_member against a delete route (test-quality issue)

Test for 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' uses PUT instead of DELETE for remove_member route, so it raises UrlGenerationError or hits add_members and never exercises the can_not_modify_automatic branch or verifies the 422 status

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the admin route is `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`, so the correct HTTP verb for the endpoint is DELETE. However, the spec in `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is a controller spec and uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which directly invokes the `remove_member` action with a PUT request and does not go through Rails route recognition. Therefore it will not raise `UrlGenerationError` nor will it "hit add_members"; it will still execute `remove_member` and can still exercise `can_not_modify_automatic` and assert 422. The finding’s claimed failure mode is not verifiable from this diff (though the verb mismatch makes the test less realistic).

adjudication_records.issue_text: New add_members action silently skips unknown usernames, but the tests pinning this behavior ('succeeds silently when adding non-existent users' / 'removing non-members') were deleted rather than ported, leaving the silent-skip branch with zero coverage

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::GroupsController#add_members the code explicitly skips unknown usernames: `if user = User.find_by_username(username) group.add(user) end`, so non-existent users are ignored without error. In the previous spec suite, this silent behavior was covered under the old PATCH-based incremental update tests (`"succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"` and `"succeeds silently when removing non-members"`), but those examples were removed and no equivalent tests were added for the new `add_members` / `remove_member` endpoints. The new specs only cover adding valid users and automatic-group rejection, leaving the silent-skip path untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The rewritten update action's non-automatic branch (accepting flat params[:name], dropping usernames, alias_level handling) is untested — no test renames a non-automatic group or verifies old nested-param callers' breakage

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, Admin::GroupsController#update was rewritten to accept flat params (params[:alias_level], params[:visible], params[:name]) and it no longer reads the previous nested payload (params[:group]) nor supports usernames updates. The specs were also rewritten and now only test that name changes are ignored for automatic groups; there is no remaining test that a non-automatic group can be renamed/updated via the new flat-param API, and the previous tests that exercised the old nested-param update path were removed. While actual external-caller breakage is not directly shown, the lack of test coverage for the non-automatic update behavior and the removed regression coverage for the old param shape are verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for the add_members error path (render_json_error) or for group.save failing after adds; the entire failure branch is untested dead code as both tests only assert be_success

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an error branch in `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` (`render_json_error(group)` when `group.save` fails), and the accompanying specs only cover the automatic-group 422 path and a successful add-members path. However, this is a test-coverage observation, not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff. Also, calling it “dead code” is not grounded in the diff: the branch is reachable if `group.save` can fail, so it’s not dead—just untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The public GroupsController#members rewrite (pagination limit/offset and new meta envelope) has no spec coverage, even though the frontend findMembers hard-depends on result.meta.total/limit/offset — contract drift could cause NaN pagination in the admin UI undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff rewrites `GroupsController#members` to return `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }` and the JS `Group#findMembers` now reads `result.meta.total/limit/offset` and `result.members`. In the provided diff, only `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` is touched; there is no spec added/updated for the public `GroupsController#members` endpoint. However, this is a test-coverage concern rather than a verifiable functional bug introduced by the diff itself—the backend and frontend contract are updated together here, so nothing in the diff shows an actual contract mismatch or NaN pagination happening.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members endpoint /groups/:group_id/users removed and response shape changed from bare array to {members: [...], meta: {...}} with no deprecation window, breaking existing consumers during rolling deploys

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the public GroupsController#members response from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (a bare JSON array) to a wrapped object `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`. The JS client is updated accordingly (Group.findMembers now expects `result.members` and `result.meta`). There is no backward-compatible handling for old clients/consumers that still expect an array, so during rolling deploys or for external API consumers this is a real breaking change. However, the specific claim that `/groups/:group_id/users` was removed is not supported by this diff (the endpoint shown is `/groups/:group_id/members`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Rewritten admin groups update action silently drops membership changes: old clients sending PUT group[usernames] or PATCH changes payloads get a success response while membership changes are not applied

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff removes handling of both the old nested payload (`payload = params[:group]` with `payload[:usernames]`) and the PATCH incremental membership changes (`params[:changes]` in `update_patch`). The new `update` only reads top-level `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` (and explicitly no usernames/membership). Therefore, an old client sending `PUT /admin/groups/:id` with `group[usernames]=...` (or `PATCH` with `changes[add]/changes[delete]`) will have those params ignored; `group.save` can still succeed and return `success_json`, while membership changes are not applied. Membership updates were moved to new endpoints `add_members`/`remove_member` (`PUT/DELETE .../members.json`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Atomic cutover of frontend group save (asJSON no longer includes usernames) with new member endpoints means mixed-version deploys can silently lose group membership edits with a 200 response

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The diff changes the contract for updating groups: the frontend no longer sends usernames on save (admin-group controller now calls group.save()/group.create(), and Group.asJSON no longer includes usernames), and membership changes move to new PUT/DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members.json endpoints. On the backend, Admin::GroupsController#update no longer reads params[:group] at all; it only looks at top-level params[:alias_level], params[:visible], params[:name]. If an older frontend is deployed against this new backend, it will still PUT data shaped like {group: {name, alias_level, visible, usernames}}. The new backend will ignore these nested params, call group.save anyway, and return success_json (200), silently dropping both the intended attribute updates and any membership edits (since usernames are ignored). This is a verifiable mixed-version cutover hazard directly implied by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id) instead of destroying the GroupUser record, skipping callbacks/side effects that the add path triggers, causing data drift

adjudication.rationale: In the new Admin::GroupsController#remove_member, membership removal is done via `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails, `association.delete` removes the join row(s) without instantiating/destroying the join model and skips `destroy` callbacks. This is also inconsistent with the prior code in the diff, which removed members via `group.remove(user)` (in the old patch-based update path), and the add path still uses `group.add(user)`. Switching to `delete` can therefore bypass any side effects implemented in `Group#remove` or join-model callbacks, making the finding a reasonable, verifiable correctness concern introduced by this change.
